</details>

LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This PKGBUILD builds the goose-desktop application from its upstream source. The source URL points to the project's own GitHub repository (`aaif-goose/goose`), and the b2sum is provided and non-SKIP. The `prepare()` function performs a single `sed` operation to auto-hide the menu bar on Linux — standard for Electron desktop apps. The `build()` and `package()` functions use conventional build tools (cargo, pnpm, just) and install files into the standard `$pkgdir` layout.

The launcher script created in `package()` reads a user-controlled flags file (`~/.config/goose-desktop-flags.conf`) and passes its contents as CLI arguments to the Electron binary. This is a well-established pattern for allowing users to customize Electron app flags (e.g., Wayland-related flags). The file is user-controlled, and the sed/tr pipeline simply strips comments and normalizes whitespace — no arbitrary code execution or data exfiltration is introduced.

No obfuscated code, unexpected network requests, dangerous commands (curl/wget/eval), or suspicious file operations were found. The package does not modify system files outside its own scope.
</details>
<evidence>
</evidence>
<summary>PkgBUILD follows standard AUR packaging practices; no malicious indicators found.</summary>
